learn.title: Carbon Markets: Clean Energy Incentives
learn.intro: Carbon markets create economic incentives to reduce emissions by assigning a price to carbon. This drives investment in clean energy projects, accelerating the transition away from fossil fuels.
learn.c1_text: Carbon credits allow companies to offset emissions by funding projects that reduce CO2. Each credit represents 1 ton of CO2 avoided. For example, renewable energy projects earn credits sold to polluters needing offsets.
learn.c2_text: Cap-and-trade systems set emission limits, letting companies buy/sell allowances. The EU’s Emissions Trading System (ETS) covers 40% of its emissions, reducing them by 38% since 2005.
learn.c3_text: India plans a voluntary carbon market to fund solar projects. With 120 GW renewable capacity (2024), it could generate 100 million tons of carbon credits annually by 2030.
learn.stat3: EU ETS covers 30% of emissions (cap 2.25 billion tons/year)

learn.title: Wind Turbine Blade Recycling
learn.intro: Wind turbine blades last 20–25 years but are hard to recycle. Innovations in material recovery and repurposing are critical to reducing waste and supporting sustainable wind energy growth.
learn.c1_text: Most blades end up in landfills due to composite materials. A 120-meter blade weighs 10 tons, equivalent to 30 cars. Only 5% are recycled globally, with costs exceeding $1M per ton.
learn.c2_text: Pyrolysis and mechanical shredding break down blades into fibers for use in cement or new composites. Denmark aims to recycle 100% of blades by 2030, creating 3,000 jobs in the process.
learn.c3_text: India has 1,000+ wind turbines, but no blade recycling infrastructure. Policies like the 2023 Renewable Energy Waste Management Rules mandate producer responsibility for end-of-life components.
learn.stat4: Cement industry uses 75% of recycled blade materials

learn.title: Solar Panel Types Compared
learn.intro: Monocrystalline, polycrystalline, and thin-film solar panels differ in efficiency, cost, and use cases. Choosing the right type impacts solar project viability and return on investment.
learn.c1_text: Monocrystalline panels (20–22% efficiency) outperform polycrystalline (15–17%) and thin-film (10–12%). A 5 kW monocrystalline system generates 28 kWh/day vs. 22 kWh/day for polycrystalline.
learn.c2_text: Monocrystalline costs 10–15% more than polycrystalline but lasts longer. Thin-film is cheaper but requires 50% more roof space. India’s solar parks use monocrystalline for high-density installations.
learn.c3_text: India’s 63 GW solar capacity (2024) includes 40% monocrystalline. The 2022 Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme boosts domestic manufacturing of all panel types.

learn.title: Geothermal Energy Basics
learn.intro: Geothermal energy harnesses Earth’s heat for power and heating. It provides reliable baseload energy with minimal emissions, making it a key player in decarbonization.
learn.c1_text: Hot subsurface water drives turbines to generate electricity. The Geysers in California produce 900 MW, enough for 750,000 homes, using steam from 10,000-year-old reservoirs.
learn.c2_text: Geothermal heat pumps transfer ground heat for building HVAC. In Iceland, 90% of homes use geothermal heating, cutting fossil fuel use by 95% in urban areas.
learn.c3_text: India has 340 MW installed geothermal capacity, mainly in Himachal Pradesh. The 2021 National Geothermal Mission targets 1 GW by 2030, leveraging 300+ hotspots.
learn.stat2: Geothermal heat pumps cut energy use by 40–60%

learn.title: Solid-State Battery Advantages
learn.intro: Solid-state batteries replace liquid electrolytes with solid materials, offering higher energy density, faster charging, and improved safety. They are pivotal for EVs and grid storage.
learn.c1_text: Solid-state batteries eliminate flammable liquid electrolytes, reducing fire risks. Toyota’s prototypes achieve 0% thermal runaway incidents vs. 0.001% in lithium-ion batteries.
learn.c2_text: Solid-state batteries store 2–3x more energy per kg than lithium-ion. A 100 kWh EV pack could weigh 500 kg (solid-state) vs. 1,000 kg (current EVs), extending range by 50%.
learn.c3_text: India’s EV market aims for 30% penetration by 2030. The 2023 Production Incentive scheme prioritizes solid-state R&D, targeting 1.5M electric vehicles using domestic batteries annually.
learn.stat2: Solid-state energy density: 500 Wh/kg (vs. 250 Wh/kg for Li-ion)

learn.title: Solar PV and the Photoelectric Effect
learn.intro: Solar panels convert sunlight into electricity via the photoelectric effect. This process enables decentralized energy generation, reducing reliance on centralized grids.
learn.c1_text: Photons strike silicon atoms, knocking electrons loose to create current. A single panel generates 300–400 W, enough to power a fridge (150 W) for 2–3 hours daily.
learn.c2_text: Panel angle, shading, and temperature affect output. Tilting panels at 15–30° optimizes yield. In Delhi, angled panels produce 20% more energy than flat installations.
learn.c3_text: India added 11 GW solar capacity in 2023, reaching 63 GW total. The 2015 solar mission targets 500 GW by 2030, with rooftop installations growing at 25% annually.
